title: Lecture 1 — Practice Exam B: Applications
subject: Programming Languages
description: Lecture 1 only. Original AI-generated practice questions based on the supplied handout; not an official exam or answer key.

questions.question: A developer must choose a language for a new project. Which benefit of studying language concepts directly helps?
options: A better basis for selecting an appropriate language
A guarantee that one language fits every project
The ability to ignore the application's domain
questions.correctAnswer: A better basis for selecting an appropriate language
questions.explanation: The lecture lists improved background for choosing languages as a reason to study their concepts.

questions.question: A service runs continuously and must use computing resources efficiently. Which domain best fits the lecture's description?
questions.explanation: Systems programming emphasizes efficiency because the software is used continuously; C and C++ are examples.

questions.question: Which domain is associated with symbol manipulation and linked lists in the lecture?
questions.explanation: The lecture associates AI with symbolic processing and lists LISP, Scheme, Prolog, and Python.

questions.question: A language offers many different ways to increment one variable. Which readability concern does this illustrate?
questions.explanation: Several constructs for the same action increase the number of forms a reader must understand.

questions.question: A team uses self-descriptive keywords instead of obscure symbols. Which criterion does this most directly support?
questions.explanation: The lecture's syntax considerations include meaningful keywords and constructs whose form reflects their meaning.

questions.question: A library exposes a simple operation while hiding a complicated implementation. Which writability feature is demonstrated?
questions.explanation: Users can express an operation without knowing all of its internal details.

questions.question: A concise increment operator replaces a longer assignment expression. Which characteristic does the lecture use this to illustrate?
questions.explanation: Expressivity includes convenient ways of specifying operations, such as a concise increment form.

questions.question: A compiler reports an incompatible operand type before the program runs. Which reliability feature is involved?
questions.explanation: Type checking detects type errors, preferably at compile time according to the lecture.

questions.question: Changing data through one reference unexpectedly changes what another reference sees. What is the likely cause?
questions.explanation: Both references may point to the same memory location, so a change through either affects the shared data.

questions.question: Why can an unreliable language implementation increase total project cost?
options: Run-time errors always reduce training costs
Defective software can cause losses and additional correction costs
questions.correctAnswer: Defective software can cause losses and additional correction costs
questions.explanation: The lecture includes reliability-related losses and maintenance in the ultimate total cost.

questions.question: What language property most strongly supports portability according to the lecture?
questions.explanation: Standardized definitions reduce differences between implementations and make movement easier.

questions.question: A language is useful across many kinds of applications. Which evaluation property is this?
questions.explanation: Generality means applicability to a wide range of applications.

questions.question: Which two factors does the lecture identify as basic influences on language design?
options: Computer architecture and program design methodologies
questions.correctAnswer: Computer architecture and program design methodologies
questions.explanation: Architecture and software development methods shape language constructs and paradigms.

questions.question: A designer wants language constructs that mirror moving results back into memory. Which imperative construct fits?
questions.explanation: In the lecture's architectural analogy, assignment statements model the movement of values to memory.

questions.question: Which sequence matches the fetch-execute cycle shown in the lecture?
options: Fetch, increment the counter, decode, execute
Decode, execute, fetch, initialize every time
questions.correctAnswer: Fetch, increment the counter, decode, execute
questions.explanation: After initializing the program counter, the slide repeatedly fetches, increments, decodes, and executes.

questions.question: Which combination describes the object-oriented methodology in the lecture?
questions.explanation: The methodology slide describes object orientation as data abstraction plus inheritance and polymorphism.

questions.question: A program expresses unordered rules rather than a sequence of assignments. Which category best fits?
questions.explanation: The lecture describes logic programming as rule-based and gives Prolog as its example.

questions.question: A language's powerful symbols make programs compact but hard to understand. Which trade-off is illustrated?
questions.explanation: APL is the lecture's example of concise expression at a readability cost.

questions.question: Which compiler phase builds a hierarchical representation of syntactic structure?
questions.explanation: Syntax analysis transforms lexical units into parse trees representing program structure.

questions.question: A JIT system compiles a subprogram on its first call. What happens to that machine-code version afterward?
options: It must be discarded before the second call
It becomes the original source text
It is turned into a markup document
It is kept for subsequent calls
questions.correctAnswer: It is kept for subsequent calls
questions.explanation: JIT retains the compiled machine-code version so subsequent calls can reuse it.
